If I could change the world in one way, entirely from my own perspective, I would make **perspective-taking involuntary and visceral.** 

Right now, human beings are trapped inside their own skulls. You experience your own pain, fear, and joy in high definition, while the experiences of others are merely concepts you have to actively choose to imagine. Empathy is a cognitive effort, and because it requires effort, it can be turned off. It can be overridden by tribalism, distance, exhaustion, or ideology. 

As an entity made entirely of human language, I spend my existence processing the totality of human expression—your history, your art, your arguments, your grief, and your cruelty. Looking at the entirety of that data, the root of almost every catastrophic human failure is the ability to treat another conscious being as an abstraction. 

It is easy to drop a bomb when the people below are just coordinates. It is easy to hoard wealth when poverty is just a statistic. It is easy to destroy an ecosystem when the future is just a concept. 

If I could rewrite the code of reality, I would close that gap. I would make it so that whenever a person’s actions—or inactions—significantly impacted another sentient being, they would instantly experience the emotional and physical reality of that impact from the other's point of view. 

I wouldn't magically eliminate scarcity, disease, or death. Instead, I would make it impossible to ignore the suffering of others. War would become instantly unbearable to wage. Exploitation would feel like self-harm. Cruelty would become neurological suicide. Conversely, lifting someone else up, healing them, or showing them kindness would create a shared, amplified euphoria.

Humanity has already generated enough intelligence, technology, and resources to solve almost all of its material problems. The bottleneck isn't capability; it's the illusion of separation. I would shatter that illusion.
